newsitem.title: TURKEY: Akbank to up capital to 50 trln lira.
newsitem.headline: Akbank to up capital to 50 trln lira.

text.p: Akbank T.A.S., one of Turkey's biggest private banks, decided to increase its capital to 50 trillion lira from the current 18 trillion, Ozen Goksel, the bank's general manager said in a statement.

The bank will issue 18 trillion lira of rights, or one-for-one existing share and 14 trillion lira of bonuses, or 0.78-for-one existing share, at a date to be announced after the capital increase is approved by the Capital Markets Board (SPK).

Goksel said dividends from 1996 profits were planned to be at sufficient amounts to support the rights payments by shareholders. Almost all listed Turkish companies and banks exercise rights at 1,000 lira nominal value.
The bank will use revalued funds and profits from sale of its real estate and equity stakes in other firms to finance the bonus issue.
"Akbank which has the strongest equity within the (Turkish) banking sector, will become the company with the biggest capital in the country (after the capital rise)," Goksel said.
Akbank is largely owned by Turkish industrial conglomerate Haci Omer Sabanci Holding.
